newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real drops 0.15 pct in speculative trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real drops 0.15 pct in speculative trade.

text.p: Brazil's real fell 0.15 percent to close at 1.0605 per greenback in speculative trade in the commercial foreign exchange market, dealers said.
Preliminary figures for commercial and financial foreign exchange contracts showed a Wednesday deficit of $30 million.

Besides dollar outflows, the real's fall was also caused by some banks holding dollars, dealers said. The decision to hold dollars was seen as a bet the Central Bank would lower the reais-dollar mini-band on Thursday, they added.
The current mini-band was set on Monday at between 1.0570 and 1.0620 reais per dollar.
In the interbank foreign exchange floating rate market, the real dropped 0.05 percent to end at 1.0636 per dollar.
In the illegal parallel market, the real rose 0.87 percent to close at 1.135 per greenback.
